_about: The one project config. Every tool in the kit reads it from the project folder; change this file, never the kit. No secrets here: keys_file only points to where the keys live (a file outside git). Every field except name and site_url is optional: a tool that needs a missing field says which one, and a check that needs one is printed as SKIP, never passed. Keys starting with an underscore are notes.
name: {{name}}
_stack: static (any site: live-page checks only) or nextjs (also runs the checks that read a Next.js repo: kit/adapters/nextjs). Other stacks get 'SKIP <id>: no adapter for <stack>' for those checks.
_site_repo: Folder of the site's code, relative to this folder (or absolute). Empty = no checkout: only the live-page and project checks run.
_site_dir: A static site with no checkout: the folder of its files, relative to this folder. Only used to date the page's last change, so evidence (screenshots, click-through, share preview) can be checked for being newer.
_commit_identity: The git identity commits to the site repo must carry (rule 118; checks repo.commit-identity and proc.commit-identity, any stack with a site checkout). Set email for a private repo whose commits carry the owner's own identity on purpose. Empty email = the kit's default: every commit must use a GitHub noreply address. email_sha256 (2.6.0) names the identity by the sha256 of the lower-case address, so a private address never has to be written into a project file; when set it wins over email (echo -n you@example.com | shasum -a 256).
_commit_style: Rule 123 (check repo.commit-style). since (2.6.0): a date such as 2026-11-22; commits made before it are history and are not checked or rewritten (no force push, no rebase of shared branches). Empty = every branch commit is checked.
_components: Where the site keeps its shared parts, for the checks that read the site's code on any stack (2.6.0): the one copy component, the '+' link-preview card, the sticky bar, the call dialog, the exit offer and the circled Tick, each a path from the site repo (src/components/frame/CopyOpen.astro). link_cards_css_class is the card's class prefix (lc for .lc .lc__title); link_cards_marker an attribute the page carries when the card is drawn; tests is a list of globs for the site's test files. Every key is optional: a part with no path is found by its file name under src/ (kebab or Pascal case: copy-button / CopyOpen, link-cards / LinkCard, sticky-cta / StickyCta, call-dialog / CallDialog, exit-offer / ExitOffer, tick / Tick); on Next.js the old components/*.tsx paths are the default; tests default to **/*.test.*, tests/** and e2e/**.
_link_graph: Checks links.inbound, links.plan, links.up-across, links.anchor-unique and links.no-redirect read inventory/link-graph.db on a stack that is not Next.js (2.6.0). The graph is fresh when its last crawl is newer than the site's last commit and no older than max_age_hours; otherwise the check prints a blocked SKIP naming the command: growth link_graph crawl --base <preview URL>. locale_prefixes: language folders the crawl joins into one page.
_branch_prefixes: The branch prefixes work may happen on (check repo.branch, Next.js adapter). An entry ending in / or - is used as written ("review-" allows review-header); any other entry gets a / ("fix" means "fix/"). Default: the kit's four.
_old_hosts: Retired host names and old server addresses that must never appear in a page, its markup, links or sitemap (rule 78; technical SEO URL-11 and LNK-08).
_spelling: The one spelling the whole site uses (rule 93). Word lists: en-US, en-CA, en-GB. A different locale per path: {"/": "en-CA", "/en-us/": "en-US"}; "html_lang" reads each page's own lang. Brand and trade words go in spelling_allow (or spelling_allow_file). Any other locale makes that check SKIP.
_keys_file: Path of the keys file, outside git (for example ~/.config/growth/<site>.env, mode 600). Never put a key in this file.

connectors._about: Each connector is off until you switch it on AND its keys are in keys_file. A missing key gives one plain note, never a crash.

_timezone: The zone the owner reads times in (for example America/New_York). Journal, tasks and the release line use it.
_conversion_path: The one page every call to action leads to (booking, quote or contact).
_booking_hosts: Extra outside booking hosts that must never be linked directly (a pasted booking link breaks rule 32). Well-known hosts (Calendly, Cal.com, Zoom, HubSpot meetings) are always checked.
_design: How the gate finds this site's page parts when its markup has no semantic signal (landmarks, ARIA, schema.org, <time datetime>, rel=author): {concept: CSS selector}. Concepts: site_header, site_footer, main, cover_image, byline, updated_date, reading_aid, faq_section, faq_question, table_source, calculator, read_next, disclosure. Selectors: tag, .class, #id, [attr], [attr=v], [attr^=v], [attr*=v], descendant (space), comma lists (kit/tools/gatelib/design.py).
_design_exceptions: A gate check that does not fit this site's design, or a site-wide fault tracked as its own task: [{"check": "<id>", "why": "<reason>", "task": "T5", "until": "<date at most 30 days ahead>"}]. It counts only after the owner approves it in their own terminal (growth approve exception <id>); editing it afterwards cancels the approval. Printed as a WARN with the reason in every gate run; it FAILs again once the task is done or the date has passed. Evidence (ev.*) and process (proc.*) checks, and a check that could not run (page did not load, input missing), are never excused.
_disclosure_pattern: A regular expression that matches this site's own 'who we are' line in a review or comparison, when the business does not make the tools it compares (for example a partner or reseller): rule 16.
_box_ignore: Components whose numbers are computed or shared, skipped by claims.box-numbers: [{"selector": ".price-calculator", "why": "its sums are computed from the table above"}]. Anything marked data-calculator is skipped always.
_booking_allowed: The site's OWN booking links that it uses on purpose, each {"match": "<part of the link>", "why": "<the reason>"}, for example {"match": "calendly.com/example-team/", "why": "the booking dialog's 'Pick a time' button opens it"}. Rule 32 then prints a WARN naming the exception instead of a FAIL; any other booking link still FAILs.

cta._about: The one call to action. label: the one text on every primary button. contact_path: the plain contact page. reason_words: words a reason line beside a button talks about (regex alternatives). events, components: dataLayer events and shared components the Next.js adapter looks for. color, color_pressed, color_token: the one CTA colour (Next.js adapter).

features._about: House components the rulebook asks for. Turn each on (true, or an object with its settings) once the site has it. One left off needs its fit reason in features_dropped (rule 161), or house.features fails.

_site_layout: Every stack: retired_paths = address prefixes that answer 410 on purpose, for example ["/tag"] (rule 76); redirect_files = files holding the redirects (rule 75 and the link map); posts_dir, pages_dir = the Markdown folders (default content/posts, content/pages); content_reader = the one module that reads the content files (rule 104, Next.js adapter). Older growth.json files keep these under "nextjs": that place is still read, but the top level wins.

nextjs._about: Only for stack nextjs: how this site's code is laid out, so the adapter's checks fit it. Every key is optional; a check that needs a setting you leave empty prints SKIP with the key to set. production_branch and remote: the branch the site is published from (default main, else master; default remote origin; with no such remote the local branch is used). start_date: when the project began (default: the steps log's first row, else the first commit). hub_files, template_files, related_posts_file, related_generic_tags: see kit/adapters/nextjs/link_map.py.

words._about: The business's own word lists, as regular-expression alternatives. Empty = that check is SKIP.
words._never_claims_allow: Exceptions to never_claims: [{"pattern": "regex", "paths": "glob such as */companies/", "why": "reason"}]. A never-claim hit on a page whose path fits the glob, whose matched words (with a little text around them) also match the pattern, is a WARN that names the why, not a FAIL. Example: our own row on a third-party comparison list may show a rate as that site states it. Any other hit still FAILs.
words._no_customers_allow_paths: Globs of pages that may use the words 'case study' in their own H1, nav and breadcrumb (a path holding 'case-stud' always may). Customer names stay banned.
words._implied_proof_allow: Implied-proof wording the owner approved for this site (logged in BRAND.md's permission log): [{"pattern": "trusted by", "why": "reason"}]. The pattern is one of the kit's built-in ones ("trusted by", "case stud(y|ies)", "teams like yours", "customers love", "award[- ]winning", "★") or a regex for the matched words; a pattern "aggregateRating" lets structured data carry a rating. An entry without a why is a FAIL. Customer names stay banned: words.hidden_customers is always checked, also after an allowed 'trusted by'. Empty = nothing changes.

_silos: Topic sections: {"first-folder-of-the-address": "Label"}. Each silo's top page is a money page.
_old_brand_words: Words of a previous brand or site, as 'one|two'. Doctor A2 and the word check fail while any is left in the project folder or the built site (build_dir). Lines that ban the words (BRAND.md 'never ...') and the steps log, which quotes the owner, do not count.
_approvals: Off by default. The owner may let the lead agent approve LOCAL work (decision, review, exception, answer, baseline) with growth approve <kind> <id> --delegated, with no terminal. Fill owner_words (the owner's own words) and since (the date) when turning it on. The log marks those lines delegated; the research browser, Google region and any go-live or release act are never delegated.
_migration: Rebuilding a site that is still live elsewhere? Set on to true and name the task that moves the pages (for example "T4"). A 404 internal link whose path is in inventory/inventory.json (growth inventory, the live site's pages) is then a WARN that names the task, not a FAIL (LNK-02). A 404 to a path the live site does not have still FAILs. Turn it off at go-live.
_build_dir: The folder of the site's production build (for example dist or out), relative to site_repo or absolute. Doctor A2 searches its pages for old_brand_words. Empty = the site is not searched (site_dir is used for a static site with no checkout).

market._about: Asked first in onboarding. Every search, AI-answer check and keyword volume uses the primary market unless a check says otherwise.

research_browser._about: true = no job with a research step starts until the research browser (Claude in Chrome) is connected and Google is set to the target country, both confirmed (doctor A14, growth wizard). Set false only for a project that never researches on the web.

_live_site_rule: no-crawl = never read the live site page by page (sitemap and robots.txt only); the agent's permissions then deny a direct fetch of the site. crawl-ok = allowed. Set by the setup wizard.
_deploy_commands: Commands the agent must never run (deploy or ship scripts); the permissions block denies each one.
_build_cmd: The site's local build and preview commands (found by the setup wizard from the repo).
_default_author: {"name": "", "role": "", "path": "/author/<slug>", "slug": ""}: the one author every page names (rule 36l). Empty = SKIP.

schema_types._about: The schema.org type of a money page's main node (rule 95). Set the one type the business is (Service for a service company). Organization, WebSite, BreadcrumbList and WebPage never count, because every page carries them.

_preview_url: The one address the owner sees previews on. Empty = the golden-rule guard (ready, url_guard) is off.
_preview_cmd: The site's own command that serves the PRODUCTION build locally (for example the framework's preview command), when growth serve <dist> does not fit (a site that renders on a server). READY must run on a production build, never a dev server (rule 106).
_preview_repo: The worktree the page is built in. Required when site_repo is set: READY and the evidence dates read this folder, not the main site checkout.
_checkpoints_extra: A Markdown file of your own page rules, one per bullet, that no gate check runs. preflight adds them to research/<key>-checkpoints.md as manual checks; each must be ticked with a proof (' -- <what you saw>') before growth ready passes.

evidence._fresh_on: When evidence (shots, click test, share preview) counts as current: 'built' (default) = the page and every CSS/JS file it links are unchanged; 'page_html' = the page's own markup is unchanged, shared bundles may differ (a site where every merged page rebuilds one shared bundle). The measured layout checks still run live on every gate.

_evidence: What makes a page's screenshots, click-test and share preview stale: the newest commit that touched the page's own content file(s) (page_tracker.page_sources or content_globs, or evidence.content_globs, each {glob, address, values}) or shared code that renders it. shared_paths (null = the default: src/components, src/layouts, src/styles, styles, src/lib, src/data, astro.config.*) replaces that list. A commit that only touches other pages' content does not count. A page whose own files cannot be found falls back to the newest commit of the whole checkout.
_contrast_cache: The contrast check (ui.contrast-states, rule 36j) keeps what it measured under <project>/.cache/contrast, keyed by the control's look-alike signature, the width and a hash of every stylesheet, so the header, footer and pills that repeat on every page are measured once, not on every page. Any CSS change gives new keys by itself. Set false to measure every control on every run (growth gate page --no-cache and growth contrast_check --no-cache do the same for one run). The cache folder keeps itself out of git.
_phone_parallel: The phone check (ui.phone, rule 70) measures its four widths side by side in one browser (about 4 s instead of 14). Set false to measure them one after the other, for a machine too busy to load four pages at once (growth phone_check --serial does the same for one run).
_thin_ok_paths: Pages that are short by nature (an author page): [{"glob": "*/author/*/", "why": "an author page lists a bio and posts"}]. A matching page gets a WARN, not a FAIL, on CNT-01 and JSR-02. An entry without a why is ignored. Default empty: no blanket exception.
_indexing: After a page is live, growth index <urls> sends it to the provider: freshlycited (FreshlyCited, paid credits, smart mode), indexnow (free; Bing and others, not Google) or manual (prints the Search Console steps). off = nothing is sent. The key lives in keys_file (outside git), never here. max_pages_per_day is a hard cap.

features_dropped._about: A house feature switched off in features needs its fit reason here (rule 161), for example {"exit_offer": "the site sells nothing online; no booking path"}. Without one, house.features fails: a reader-visible feature is never dropped silently.

layout._about: The measured design limits of rule 158a (layout.*, cta.one-per-view, cta.spacing, cta.legal-quiet, engage.one-mechanic). Every key is optional; these are the defaults. A limit changed for one site needs a "_why" next to it.

links._not_text: Regex alternatives for a site's own menu, contents or badge link classes that are not running text (rule 36c, links.blue).
